## Objective
- Increase the map in “Frontline: Global Command” another 20× and buildings 10× while keeping gameplay playable.

## Requirements
- Apply scale changes consistently without asking clarifying questions; briefly note reasonable assumptions when finished.
- Verify the game in-browser and save and inspect only the latest small JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Treat the unfinished request saved in `.omgithub/conversation.json` as the active scale request.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected world sizing, camera and coordinate scaling, building models, placement and selection logic, and gameplay movement.

### Active
- Implement map and building scale changes while maintaining navigation, placement, selection, and playability.
- Run and verify the game in-browser; save and inspect a JPEG screenshot at viewport ≤1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Increase map dimensions and update world-to-screen scaling and camera sizing consistently in `game.js` and `renderer3d.js`.
2. Increase building model scale and adjust placement/select hit testing and spacing to match.
3. Run and verify the game in-browser; save and inspect a JPEG screenshot at viewport ≤1280px.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World size, zoom, normalized coordinates, placement validation, selection hit testing, and gameplay movement.
- `renderer3d.js`: World dimensions, camera view, terrain, and building model scale.
- `index.html`: Game UI and map controls.
- `styles.css`: Game layout and viewport sizing.
- `.omgithub/conversation.json`: Saved wording of the active scale request.

## Important Context
- No code changes or browser verification have been completed.
- Current values: `WORLD_SIZE = 448`, `MAP_SCALE = WORLD_SIZE / 160`, `ZOOM_MIN = .28`, `ZOOM_MAX = 2.2`; renderer uses `WORLD = 448`, `VIEW_SIZE = 160`.
- Building sizes are 29–45; renderer model scaling uses `Math.max(.35, entity.size / 70)`.
- Placement obstruction checks use building size plus 30; selection hit testing uses actor size or radius plus a pointer margin.
- Terrain and camera position are normalized against a fixed 448-unit renderer world.
